projectTitle: Carnegie Mellon: One CMS for the flagship and the unit sites
project_haiku: Carnegie Mellon needed the flagship site and the department sites to share a design system without sharing a single editor. We built that distribution on Drupal, GitLab, and Pantheon, with CMU reviewing every merge.
project_footer_CTA: Need unit sites that can publish on their own and still look like the university? That is the system we built with Carnegie Mellon.
pageSummary:
The job

Carnegie Mellon and Carnegie Higher Ed set out to replace a web presence that had become hard to govern. Departments needed to publish on their own. The university needed one brand, one component set, and a path from a reviewed merge to production. The work ran about eighteen months.

What we built

Knectar implemented the Drupal distribution. Development sits in GitLab. Hosting is a Pantheon upstream. A feature is a merge request that CMU's own developers review before it reaches the pipeline. The flagship, cmu.edu, and the unit sites draw on the same components.

Outcomes

A department can run its site. A change to the system still passes through CMU's review before it is on the public web.
